speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what the vertigo feels like—does the room seem to be spinning, or do you feel lightheaded and unsteady?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Did you experience any accompanying symptoms such as hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or difficulty speaking or walking?
REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient’s symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you experience any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness in the left ear?
REQUEST TEST: Audiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Within normal limits for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver on the left side and normal hearing, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
